corpus.evidence: fixtures are drawn from real findings on the pinned 8-repo corpus (okta-auth-js generateIdxAction.ts, request.ts) plus an adversarial wave, but no vulnerable/safe corpus is authored beside this record from the defect itself.

oracle.evidence: no independent decider. The natural one is a PARSER: text that parses as a statement list is code, text that does not is prose. That would replace the whole pattern heuristic and is the real fix this rule wants.
oracle.command: score findings by attempting to parse the comment body

effectiveFp.evidence: not met, but no longer unmeasured: the 20-repo ledger files these findings by SHAPE and now reports only 2 new cases per run, so the population is nearly closed. The n>=20 sampled adjudication has not been done.

reachability.evidence: not applicable in the taint sense; this rule reports on comment text, not on a data path.

duel.evidence: not scored against a competitor. The comparable is sonarjs S125 (commented-out code), which is the rule this one cites.

adversarial.evidence: a wave found 11 of 14 genuinely commented-out lines going silent — far more than the `// x = 1` the prose fix was documented as costing. Two causes: the terminator proxy is too blunt for unmistakable statements, and the pattern list had no `throw`, no `await` and no member-call chain. All 14 now caught with 0 prose FPs across a 9-case prose set. UNMET until a second wave finds nothing new.

realSource.evidence: measured on TWO corpora. The 8-repo pinned corpus fell 2,441 -> 143. The 20-repo ledger then read 3,557 — 25x more per repository — and the gap was the finding: JSDoc blocks were reported, because an `@example` body IS code and the rule had no reason to treat it as documentation. 3,557 -> 1,879, with the pinned corpus unchanged.

partition.evidence: not probed. Overlaps conceptually with expiring-todo-comments in the same plugin, which also reads comment text.

behaviour.evidence: scripts/rule-seal-probe.mts has not been run against this rule.

coverage.evidence: 100% statements / branches / functions / lines across eslint-plugin-conventions, 445 tests.

recorded.evidence: BENCHMARK-RESULTS.md not updated for this rule.

knownGaps.summary: the rule decides 'is this code' by pattern matching on text rather than by parsing it.
knownGaps.why: a parser is the correct oracle and the correct implementation, but swapping it in changes every number this rule has ever produced; it is a rewrite, not a patch.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: a parse-based classifier is prototyped and scored against the same corpus.

knownGaps.summary: a bare fragment with no structure and no terminator, such as `// x = 1`, is still silent.
knownGaps.why: indistinguishable from prose by any text heuristic; real commented-out code is lifted from a file and keeps its punctuation or its declaration shape.

knownGaps.summary: a sentence that happens to end in a bracket, such as `// NOTE: enableLegacyMode (via isStepMode)`, can still report.
knownGaps.why: the terminator proxy accepts it; measured as a small residual on the pinned corpus rather than eliminated.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: the parse-based classifier lands, or the residual grows.

knownGaps.summary: a JSDoc block is skipped wholesale, so genuinely commented-out code inside one is missed.
knownGaps.why: an `@example` body is the one place a comment is SUPPOSED to contain code, and nothing in the body distinguishes it from commented-out code. Deliberately narrow: only `/**` is exempt, and a plain `/* … */` — which is how people actually comment code out — is still checked.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: the parse-based classifier lands and can read the JSDoc tag structure.

notes: Sealed alongside reliability/no-missing-null-checks on 2026-08-21. Same lesson: the adversarial axis found the recall cost that the FP work had understated in its own commit message.
